subject: Specify a prior when using LKJ

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Specify a prior when using LKJ
parts:
Hi,

approximately I know the distribution for my correlation matrix,
after I figured it out in a STAN model by:

L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(4);

Eg. I know the parameter is in the range of mean + sd.
With "new" data this doesn't changes "much".

With the inverse wishart distribution I could specify a prior. 
With the preferred lkj not. 

I changed the model for every "non-fixed" parameter p_ij of the
correlation L_Omega to:

p_ij_raw ~ normal(mu_ij, sigma_ij);
p_ij = tanh(p_ij_raw);

Why is the preferred "gold-standard" of this case?

Thank you so much,
Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Specify a prior when using LKJ
parts:
Why do we prefer LKJ?

It's only a prior on the correlation matrix --- you need
a seperate prior on the scales.

We like LKJ because it has a natural interpretation of
controlling how much we expect the result to look like an
identity matrix.

The inverse Wishart has the nice property of looking like
prior data (it's conjugate for covariance matrices, so
it has to look like previously observed data).

For more info, see:

http://andrewgelman.com/2012/08/30/visualizing-distributions-of-covariance-matrices/

- Bob
